the emergence and spread of blaNDM5 and mcr1 in dairy cows in China.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blaNDM5 gene was located within a pNDM-MCR194 plasmid in three NDM5-producing E. coli isolats from cows in Jiangsu province.
the blaNDM gene is located on a pNDM-MCR194-like plasmids, while mcr gene is located on an IncHI2 plamid in the three isolates, respectively.

blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-2 were the most frequently found carbapenemase genes in Enterobacteriacea isolates from dairy farms, and the blaNDM gene-positive isolates were resistant to multiple antibiotics, and blaNDM genes were mainly carried by IncX3 plasmids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-circulation of blaNDM-positive E. coli strains and mcr- 1-positive strains is a serious threat to public health and the environment.
the blaNDM5-positive E. coil isolates in dairy cow were extensively resistant, and the blaNDM-carrying plasimds were highly transferable.
blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-2 are the most prevalent carbapenemases in E. coli from dairy farms, while blaNDM-4 and blaNDM5 are rarely found in this environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the blaNDM gene is widely distributed among E. coli isolations in China, and it is important to monitor the emergence of NDM-1 and other carbapenemases in the future.
the coexistence of mcr-1 and blaNDM-1 in the same host is likely a result of the co-selection of these resistance determinants by antimicrobials.
the emergence of blaNDM and mcr-encoding plasmids is a serious threat to public health and the food industry.
